relevance_reason: This is the first report of a patient with PNPLA8-related mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis. It describes her clinical features, compound heterozygous frameshift variants, muscle pathology and the loss of PNPLA8 protein.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) reported a 7-year-old girl (CMH193) with suspected mitochondrial myopathy. She was asymptomatic and met developmental milestones in her first year, apart from toe-walking. She had a positive Gowers sign at age 2 and could no longer walk by age 3. Her course was progressive: proximal muscle weakness, decline of fine motor skills, dysarthria, dysmetria, dystonia, hypotonia that progressed to spasticity, complex partial seizures with left temporal lobe spikes on EEG, a very lean body habitus without weight gain, and significant lactic acidosis requiring bicarbonate supplementation.
quotes: At age 2, she was noted to have a positive Gowers sign, and by the age of 3 years could no longer walk. Independent sitting was restricted to 10 minutes due to fatigue. Her fine motor skills declined and speech became dysarthric.

Hypotonicity progressed to spasticity of different opposing muscle groups. She recently developed complex partial seizures associated with recurrent left temporal lobe spikes on EEG, and slow wave discharges exacerbated by sleep.
In addition, she developed significant lactic acidosis, requiring bicarbonate supplementation.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) found that the patient had a consistently elevated anion gap from age 5, and at age 7 had elevated blood lactate (3.8-5.6 mmol/L) and pyruvate with a lactate:pyruvate ratio of 17.5-21.1. Her plasma acylcarnitines and creatine phosphokinase were normal. CSF showed deficiency of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Muscle SDH and COX activities and electron transport chain function were normal, and the authors suggested mitochondrial dysfunction rather than an electron transport chain defect.
quotes: At age 7, elevated lactic and pyruvic acid was demonstrated in blood on multiple occasions (lactic acid 3.8-5.6; n=0.7-2.1 mmol/L and pyruvic acid 0.18-0.32; n=0.08-0.16 mmol/L) with ratios of 17.5-21.1 (n=<20); plasma acylcarnitine profile was normal.
In the absence of an elevated lactate: pyruvate ratio, these results suggest mitochondrial dysfunction rather than an electron transport chain defect.
Neurotransmitter studies in cerebrospinal fluid performed at the age of 6 showed deficiency of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) reported that a muscle biopsy taken at age 4 showed variable fiber size with isolated small atrophic fibers but no ragged red fibers. Electron microscopy showed mitochondria with marked disarray of cristae, globular dense osmiophilic inclusions, and subsarcolemmal aggregates of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes, suggestive of degenerating mitochondria. Secondary lysosomes were increased. A brain MRI at 33 months showed subtle increased signal in the medial globus pallidus bilaterally, which was no longer seen two years later.
quotes: Specifically, mitochondria from CMH193 exhibit marked disarray of cristae and globular dense osmiophilic inclusions by EM analysis.

In addition, subsarcolemmal aggregates of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes and dense round or oval, strongly osmiophilic inclusions were observed, suggestive of degenerating mitochondria (Fig. 1b, c).
In addition, variable fiber size was found with isolated small atrophic fibers of all subtypes observed, but with no ragged red fibers (Fig. 1a).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter
Subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormally shaped mitochondria

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) performed trio exome sequencing and found that the patient was compound heterozygous for a frameshift variant in PNPLA8, c.334_337delAATT (p.Asn112HisfsX29), confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The variant was inherited from a carrier parent, and two healthy siblings did not carry it. It was absent from EVS and from an internal database of 1913 samples.
quotes: the patient was compound heterozygous for two frameshift variants, c.334_337delAATT (p.Asn112HisfsX29) and c.1975_1976delAG (p.Leu659AlafsX4) in PNPLA8
Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern.
Both PNPLA8 variants were absent from the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project (EVS; http://evs.gs.washington.edu/EVS/) and an internal variant database of 1913 samples.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) identified a second frameshift variant in PNPLA8 in the same patient, c.1975_1976delAG (p.Leu659AlafsX4), in compound heterozygous state. The variant was inherited from a carrier parent and was absent from EVS and an internal database.
quotes: the patient was compound heterozygous for two frameshift variants, c.334_337delAATT (p.Asn112HisfsX29) and c.1975_1976delAG (p.Leu659AlafsX4) in PNPLA8
Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) showed by Western blot that the patient's muscle had a dramatic decrease in the 88-, 63- and 52-kD iPLA2-gamma (PNPLA8) bands compared with 3 control muscles. A 110-kD band was also absent; mass spectrometry identified this band as HSPA4 reacting nonspecifically with the antibody. The authors speculated that losing this chaperone might contribute to the disease.
quotes: As predicted, Western blotting of tissue from the patient exhibited a dramatic decrease in multiple immunoreactive iPLA2γ bands known to be absent in the Pnpla8 -/- mouse.
The results demonstrated the 110 kD band to be heat shock protein family member 4 (HSPA4) (Supp. Table S2).

Western blot showing dramatic decrease of the 88, 63, and 52kD PNPLA8 protein (NP_001242940.1) in the muscle from CMH193, compared to muscle from three control samples with known non-mitochondrial diagnoses.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) noted that the patient's phenotype resembled that of Pnpla8-null mice. These mice show mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired learning, decreased exercise endurance, enhanced insulin sensitivity, a thin body habitus and cold intolerance. They also have dysmorphic mitochondria similar to those seen in the patient's muscle.
quotes: The Pnpla8 -/- mouse has mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired learning, decreased exercise endurance, enhanced insulin sensitivity, a thin body habitus (from energy dissipation by mitochondrial uncoupling), and cold intolerance.

In summary, a causal link between the proband's phenotype and PNPLA8 variantsis supported by the parallel alterations in neuromuscular dysfunction, cognitive deficits and the striking similarities in dysmorphic and degenerating mitochondria present in the Pnpla8 -/- mouse.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) suggested that in PNPLA8-related disease, as in PLA2G6-related disease, the primary mechanism may be degeneration of the mitochondrial inner membrane. In their view, electron transport proteins would be affected only secondarily, through altered membrane homeostasis.
quotes: This may also be the case with PNPLA8-related disease, where proteins involved in electron transport and ATP synthesis located in the inner membranes would be secondarily affected by altered membrane homeostasis but not the primary pathogenic mechanism.

relevance_reason: Reports two unrelated patients with biallelic loss-of-function PNPLA8 variants and a mitochondrial neurodegenerative phenotype with lactic acidosis.

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) described a female infant from India, born to consanguineous parents, who had congenital microcephaly (head circumference 29 cm, -4 SD at birth) and multifocal clonic seizures that began on day 2 of life, along with spasticity of all 4 limbs. Brain MRI showed microcephaly with a simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, a prominent cisterna magna with a hypoplastic cerebellum, and brainstem atrophy. MRS showed an elevated lipid-lactate peak. TORCH testing was negative.
quotes: A female child was evaluated on the sixth postnatal day in the neonatal intensive care unit for congenital microcephaly and seizures. She was the second born child to a consanguineous couple with a two-year old healthy female sibling (Figure 1A).

Brain MRI showed microcephaly with simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of corpus callosum, prominent cisterna magna with hypoplastic cerebellum, brainstem atrophy (Figure 2A–C). Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) showed an elevated lipid-lactate peak.
Weight was 2410 gm (−2 SD), length 48 cm (−1 SD) and head circumference 29 cm (−4 SD) at birth.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated brain lactate level by MRS

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) described a girl of India/Fiji origin, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who developed normally until about 13 months of age and then regressed, with episodes of epilepsia partialis continua and focal seizures. She stayed at an 8-month developmental level, did not speak, needed a gastrostomy tube, and developed acquired microcephaly (head circumference -4.7 SD at 15 years). Other features were hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness, absent reflexes, choreiform movements, dystonia, contractures, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with subaortic stenosis, obstructive sleep apnea, and visual evoked potentials with severely reduced amplitudes. Serial MRI showed progressive atrophy of the cerebellum, brainstem, and cerebrum with corpus callosum thinning. MRS showed a persistent lipid-lactate peak, blood lactate was elevated, and GDF15 was elevated (1293 pg/ml).
quotes: By history, she had normal development until about 13 months of age. She was able to independently sit, stand, cruise, and babble. However, she then regressed concomitantly with several episodes of epilepsy partialis continua and difficult to control focal seizures.
She developed involuntary choreiform movements, dystonia, proximal muscle weakness and absent muscle stretch reflexes. Evolving severe contractures at the hamstrings, biceps and ankles were observed.
Echocardiography detected hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with subaortic stenosis. Blood lactate was found to be elevated in several occasions.
Over the ensuing decade there was cortical volume loss in the cerebellum, brainstem, bilateral parietal and occipital lobes and corpus callosum thinning (Figure 2D–2L).

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) reported that electron microscopy of the muscle biopsy in patient 2 showed enlarged, irregularly shaped mitochondria with surrounding membrane whorls, disrupted cristae, electron-dense deposits, lipid droplets, and pools of glycogen. Activities of electron transport chain complexes I to IV were in the normal range. Mitochondrial DNA sequencing found no variation.
quotes: Muscle biopsy demonstrated enlarged and irregular shaped mitochondria on electron microscopy with surrounding membrane whorls. Electron dense deposits, lipid droplets, pools of glycogen and empty vacuoles, disrupted cristae.
Electron transport chain enzymatic activities of complexes I – IV were within normal ranges.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain

findings.statement: Whole exome sequencing by Shukla et al. (2018) identified a homozygous nonsense variant in PNPLA8, c.517G>T (p.Glu173Ter; NM_001256007.1), in patient 1, the child of consanguineous parents. Sanger sequencing showed that both parents were heterozygous for the variant.
quotes: In patient, 1 we identified a homozygous nonsense variant in PNPLA8 [(c.517G>T, p.(Glu173Ter), NM_001256007.1] (Figure 1B).
Sanger sequencing of the variant, c.517G>T [p.(Glu173Ter), NM_001256007.1] in homozygous state in patient 1 and heterozygous state in the parents (D).

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) found compound heterozygous variants in PNPLA8 in patient 2 by trio whole exome sequencing: a 2-bp deletion, c.2275_2276delCT (p.Leu759AlafsTer4), and a nonsense variant, c.419C>A (p.Ser140Ter). The variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and segregation analysis showed that each was inherited from a carrier parent.
quotes: Patient 2 was found to possess compound variants in PNPLA8, c.2275_2276delCT; p.(Leu759AlafsTer4) and c.419C>A; p.(Ser140Ter).
Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive pattern (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) noted that segregation of biallelic PNPLA8 variants from carrier parents was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive pattern (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) noted that all of the reported PNPLA8 variants introduce premature stop codons and were likely to cause truncated protein or nonsense-mediated decay. They also noted that the abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes seen in patient 2 matched findings in Pnpla8-null mice, which develop a mitochondrial neurodegenerative disorder.
quotes: The variants observed in PNPLA8, including the ones in our study are loss-of-function pathogenic variants, which introduce a premature stop codon (Figure 1E).

Histological findings in P2 of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes and inclusions were in concordance with the observations in the null-mice and the patient reported by Saunders et al..

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) noted that the clinical picture in the 3 known patients with PNPLA8 variants was similar but variable. They stated that, because so few individuals had been reported, a genotype-phenotype correlation could not yet be made.
quotes: The clinical picture in the three patients with pathogenic variants in PNPLA8 is similar but variable.
Also, due to limited number of individuals, a genotype-phenotype correlation cannot be deduced at present.

relevance_reason: Mouse knockout of iPLA2gamma (Pnpla8) showing a mitochondrial bioenergetic phenotype; animal model evidence for the PNPLA8-related mitochondrial myopathy.

findings.statement: Mancuso et al. (2007) generated mice null for iPLA2-gamma (Pnpla8) by eliminating the enzyme's active site through homologous recombination. The null mice had multiple bioenergetic dysfunctional phenotypes: growth retardation, cold intolerance, reduced exercise endurance, and greatly increased mortality from cardiac stress after transverse aortic constriction. They also had abnormal mitochondrial function, with a 65% decrease in ascorbate-induced complex IV-mediated oxygen consumption, and reduced myocardial cardiolipin content with an altered mix of cardiolipin molecular species. The authors concluded that iPLA2-gamma is essential for efficient mitochondrial bioenergetic function because it shapes mitochondrial membrane lipid metabolism and composition.
quotes: we generated mice null for the iPLA(2)gamma gene by eliminating the active site of the enzyme through homologous recombination

Mice null for iPLA(2)gamma display multiple bioenergetic dysfunctional phenotypes, including 1) growth retardation, 2) cold intolerance, 3) reduced exercise endurance, 4) greatly increased mortality from cardiac stress after transverse aortic constriction

5) abnormal mitochondrial function with a 65% decrease in ascorbate-induced Complex IV-mediated oxygen consumption, and 6) a reduction in myocardial cardiolipin content accompanied by an altered cardiolipin molecular species composition

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex IV

relevance_reason: Mouse knockout of Pnpla8 (iPLA2gamma) causes mitochondrial dysfunction and skeletal muscle myopathy, which serves as an animal model for PNPLA8-related mitochondrial myopathy.

findings.statement: Yoda et al. (2010) found that mice with a knockout of iPLA2-gamma (Pnpla8) were born at the expected Mendelian ratio and looked normal and healthy at 1 month of age. Growth retardation began at 2 months, and kyphosis and significant muscle weakness were present by 4 months. Electron microscopy of knockout skeletal muscle showed swollen mitochondria, fewer mitochondria, and atrophy of myofilaments. The knockout muscle also had increased lipid peroxidation and induction of several oxidative stress-related genes. The authors concluded that loss of iPLA2-gamma causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased oxidative stress, leading to loss of skeletal muscle structure and function.
quotes: iPLA(2)γ-knockout (KO) mice were born with an expected Mendelian ratio and appeared normal and healthy at the age of one month but began to show growth retardation from the age of two months as well as kyphosis and significant muscle weakness at the age of four months.
Electron microscopy revealed swelling and reduced numbers of mitochondria and atrophy of myofilaments in iPLA(2)γ-KO skeletal muscles.
These results provide evidence that impairment of iPLA(2)γ causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased oxidative stress, leading to the loss of skeletal muscle structure and function.

phenotypes.text: swollen and reduced mitochondria in skeletal muscle

findings.statement: In skeletal muscle from iPLA2-gamma-knockout mice, Yoda et al. (2010) found that the composition of cardiolipin and of other phospholipid subclasses was altered. Levels of myoprotective prostanoids were also reduced. The authors suggested that, besides helping maintain mitochondrial membrane homeostasis, iPLA2-gamma may contribute to modulating the production of lipid mediators in vivo.
quotes: We further found that the compositions of cardiolipin and other phospholipid subclasses were altered and that the levels of myoprotective prostanoids were reduced in iPLA(2)γ-KO skeletal muscle.
Thus, in addition to maintenance of homeostasis of the mitochondrial membrane, iPLA(2)γ may contribute to modulation of lipid mediator production in vivo.

relevance_reason: This paper reports a new patient with compound heterozygous PNPLA8 variants, describes her clinical features and muscle pathology, and reviews the published cases.

findings.statement: Chen et al. (2024) reported a 27-year-old Chinese woman whose gait became abnormal at age 11. At age 17 she still had amenorrhea and an infantile uterus, and at age 21 she developed head and limb tremors. Brain MRI suggested mild cerebellar atrophy. A biceps muscle biopsy showed mild myopathic changes on light microscopy and mitochondrial inclusions on electron microscopy.
quotes: A 27-year-old Chinese woman presented with abnormal gait at age 11, remained amenorrhoeic with an infantile uterus at age 17, and presented with head and limb tremors at age 21.
The results of brain magnetic resonance imaging suggested mild cerebellar atrophy.
Her muscle biopsy showed mild myopathic changes on light microscopy and mitochondrial inclusions on electron microscopy.

phenotypes.text: mild myopathic changes on muscle biopsy

findings.statement: In a 27-year-old Chinese woman with cerebellar ataxia, tremors, and primary ovarian insufficiency, Chen et al. (2024) used whole-exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous variants in the PNPLA8 gene: c.1777T>G (p.Tyr593Asp), a missense variant, and c.1515-1516delTT (p.Tyr506Serfs*27), a frameshift variant. She inherited the variants from her parents.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing was performed, and mitochondrial and spinal cerebellar ataxia genes were screened.
The patient's genetic screening revealed compound heterozygous variants c.1777T > G (p.Tyr593Asp) and c.1515-1516delTT (p.Tyr506Serfs*27) of PNPLA8 inherited from her parents.

findings.statement: Chen et al. (2024) reviewed 25 patients from 21 families with PNPLA8 variants. They concluded that age of onset is a very important factor in the clinical phenotype and prognosis. They also observed that adult females with PNPLA8 variants may present with primary ovarian dysfunction, and they suggested that mitochondrial inclusion bodies may be a pathologic hallmark.
quotes: A total of 25 patients from 21 families were reviewed.
Age of onset is a very important factor in terms of patient clinical phenotype and prognosis of PNPLA8-related disorders.
It has been observed that adult females with PNPLA8 variants may present with primary ovarian dysfunction. The presence of mitochondrial inclusion bodies may serve as a pathological hallmark

relevance_reason: This is a large series of patients with biallelic PNPLA8 variants. It widens the PNPLA8-related neurological spectrum, reports genotype–phenotype correlations, and includes functional organoid, mitochondrial and lipidomic studies. It is relevant to the PNPLA8 disorder entry but centres on the neurodevelopmental phenotype rather than myopathy with lactic acidosis.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) identified biallelic ultra-rare PNPLA8 variants by exome or genome sequencing in 14 individuals (6 male, 8 female; aged 3 days to 33 years) from 12 unrelated families with neurological manifestations. The 14 variants (12 novel) comprised 4 nonsense, 5 frameshift, 3 intronic variants near exon-intron boundaries, and 2 missense variants. Each had a population frequency below 0.001%. Pedigrees were consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: We identified 14 individuals (six male and eight female individuals) showing neurological manifestations from 12 unrelated families with biallelic variants in PNPLA8 (Fig. 1A).
Of the 14 variants, four were nonsense, five were frameshift, three were intronic variants near an exon–intron boundary, and two were missense variants.
the frequency of all of the variants was <0.001%, suggesting a strong purification effect attributable to disease pathogenicity.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) reported that common features in their 14 patients were central hypotonia (13/13), dystonia (8/12), seizures (10/14) and cerebellar atrophy (12/12). Eight patients (Families 1-8) were severely affected. They had congenital microcephaly (5/7), global developmental delay with no milestones attained (7/7), peripheral spasticity (7/8) and seizure onset within 7 months of age (8/8). Neuroimaging in this group showed a simplified gyral pattern (6/6), pontocerebellar hypoplasia (7/7) and severe progressive cerebral atrophy (5/5).
quotes: Highly frequent clinical features of our patients were central hypotonia (100%, 13/13), dystonia (67%, 8/12), seizure (71%, 10/14) and cerebellar atrophy (100%, 12/12).

eight patients (Families 1–8; Fig. 1B–D) were characterized further by several common features, such as congenital microcephaly (71%, 5/7), global developmental delay attaining no milestones (100%, 7/7), peripheral spasticity (88%, 7/8) and early-onset seizure within 7 months of age (100%, 8/8).

Neuroimaging revealed that these patients showed a simplified gyral pattern (100%, 6/6), pontocerebellar hypoplasia (100%, 7/7) and severe progressive atrophy of the cerebral cortex (100%, 5/5; Fig. 1E–R).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) described 4 patients from Families 11 and 12 who had a relatively mild phenotype. All attained walking (4/4) and all had regression of milestones (4/4). Ataxia was present in 3/4, intellectual disability was mild or absent in 3/4, and seizures were unique or absent in all 4. Brain MRI showed little or no cerebral volume loss but progressive cerebellar atrophy. Two patients (Families 9 and 10) were of intermediate severity.
quotes: four patients (Families 11–12) were characterized by relatively mild features: attaining the milestone of walking (100%, 4/4), ataxia (75%, 3/4), regression of milestones (100%, 4/4), mild or no intellectual disability (75%, 3/4) and unique or absent seizures (100%, 4/4).

Brain MRI showed little or no cerebral cortical volume loss but progressive cerebellar atrophy, consistent with the pronounced movement disorder observed in patients (100%, 3/3; Fig. 1V–Y and Supplementary Videos 1 and 2).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) combined their patients with 11 previously reported individuals from 8 families (25 individuals from 20 families in total). The PNPLA8-related disorder formed a continuum from developmental and/or degenerative epileptic-dyskinetic encephalopathy to childhood-onset neurodegeneration. Biallelic loss-of-function variants affecting three or four PNPLA8 protein isoforms were found specifically in the severe group with congenital microcephaly. Patients of intermediate severity carried a loss-of-function variant, missense variants or the recurrent C-terminal frameshift p.Leu759Alafs*4. All mildly affected patients, who had late-onset movement disorders, carried biallelic C-terminal frameshift variants (p.Thr757Glnfs*10 or p.Leu759Alafs*4).
quotes: Regarding their genotypes, biallelic LoF variants affecting three or four PNPLA8 protein isoforms were associated specifically with this group (Fig. 2).
These four patients carried the combination of either a LoF variant, missense variants or a recurrent frameshift variant (p.Leu759Alafs*4) located at the C-terminus (Fig. 2).
All the patients in this group harboured biallelic C-terminal frameshift variants (p.Thr757Glnfs*10 or p.Leu759Alafs*4) (Fig. 2).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that the PNPLA8 c.1625+3_1625+6del variant in Patient 1 (Family 1, a Japanese boy) caused skipping of exons 6-8 in patient lymphoblastoid cells. Skin fibroblasts from this patient showed a significant reduction of the 77-kDa PNPLA8 protein, which the authors interpreted as a null effect.
quotes: Sequencing of each separated transcript by TA cloning revealed that c.1625+3_1625+6del resulted in the skipping of exons 6–8 owing to aberrant splicing (Supplementary Fig. 1A and B).
Immunoblotting analysis for the skin fibroblasts from Patient 1 showed a significant reduction in 77-kDa PNPLA8 expression, indicating a null effect of his genetic variants (Supplementary Fig. 1C).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) identified the PNPLA8 splice variants c.2075-2A>G in Patient 2 and c.1684-2A>G in Patient 5. No patient cells were available for testing, but SpliceAI predicted loss of the splice acceptor site for each variant (delta scores 0.97 and 0.93).
quotes: However, in silico analysis with SpliceAI predicted that c.2075-2A>G and c.1684-2A>G result in the loss of a splice acceptor site with a Δ score of 0.97 and 0.93, respectively (high-specificity cut-off: 0.8).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) studied PNPLA8 protein in patient skin fibroblasts. The p.Glu296Lysfs*6 variant from severely affected Patient 6 had a null effect. Fibroblasts from Patient 12 (mild, p.Leu759Alafs*4) and Patient 14 (non-neuronal, p.Val7*) showed weak expression of the 77-kDa protein, suggesting residual function. Fibroblasts from a previously reported, severely affected patient homozygous for the missense variant p.Val520Asp expressed PNPLA8 at levels similar to controls.
quotes: We found that the LoF variant identified in the severe case (Patient 6: p.Glu296Lysfs*6) resulted in a null effect, similar to Patient 1.

In contrast, LoF variants identified in non-severe cases (Patient 12, mild phenotype with p.Leu759Alafs*4; Patient 14, non-neuronal phenotype with p.Val7*) exhibited weak expression of the 77-kDa PNPLA8 protein, suggesting residual protein function (Supplementary Fig. 2C).

the missense variant identified in the previously reported patient (severe phenotype with homozygous p.Val520Asp) resulted in a similar protein expression level to the controls despite the severe phenotype

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) identified two individuals from two unrelated Iranian families in a non-neurological cohort who were homozygous for distinct N-terminal PNPLA8 frameshift variants affecting only the 88-kDa isoform. One had optic atrophy and the other had nonsyndromic hearing loss. In the optic atrophy family, an affected sibling was only heterozygous for the variant. The authors therefore considered the significance of these variants undetermined.
quotes: A patient from one family showed optic atrophy, and the other patient showed non-syndromic hearing loss. These patients were homozygous for distinct N-terminal frameshift variants, which affect only the largest protein isoform (molecular weight 88 kDa)
It is worth noting that in the family showing optic atrophy, there was an affected sibling of the proband, while he was heterozygous for the variant (Supplementary Fig. 2B).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that cardiolipin and monolysocardiolipin levels appeared lower in patient skin fibroblasts than in controls, without a significant correlation with severity. Patient 1 fibroblasts had normal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy but significantly reduced maximal respiration.
quotes: Although a significant correlation was not observed between CL/MLCL abundance and phenotypic severity, the abundance of CL and MLCL appeared to be decreased in patient-derived skin fibroblasts compared with control samples (Supplementary Fig. 2D and E).

live-cell assessment of mitochondrial OXPHOS activity using an extracellular flux analyser revealed that the maximal respiration level was significantly lower in the patient-derived skin fibroblasts than those from healthy controls

phenotypes.text: reduced mitochondrial maximal respiration in fibroblasts
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) generated cerebral organoids from CRISPR/Cas9 PNPLA8 knockout iPSCs. At 12 weeks, these organoids had a smaller subventricular zone-like region, fewer PAX6+HOPX+ basal radial glial cells and fewer SATB2+ upper-layer neurons. Basal intermediate progenitors and deep-layer neurons were unchanged. BrdU+ cells were increased, suggesting an altered S phase.
quotes: We found that the SVZ area was smaller in PNPLA8 KO cerebral organoids compared with WT cerebral organoids at 12 weeks, whereas there was no significant difference at 8 weeks of culture (Fig. 3F and H).
The number of PAX6+HOPX+ bRGCs in the SVZ was significantly reduced in PNPLA8 KO cerebral organoids compared with WT cerebral organoids (Fig. 4A and B).
The number of SATB2+ upper-layer neurons was significantly reduced in PNPLA8 KO cerebral organoids compared with WT cerebral organoids

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that cerebral organoids from Patient 1 iPSCs reproduced the knockout organoid findings, with fewer basal radial glial cells and fewer upper-layer neurons. Spatial transcriptomics showed altered fate specification of apical radial glia and enrichment of lysophospholipid pathway genes. PNPLA8 knockout neural progenitor cells had reduced LPA, LPE and PA, with normal mitochondrial function. Adding LPA increased basal radial glial cell numbers in patient organoids.
quotes: Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids exhibited a reduced number of PAX6+HOPX+ bRGCs in the SVZ compared with Control cerebral organoids at 8 weeks of culture (Fig. 5C and D).
The amounts of LPA, LPE and PA were decreased in PNPLA8 KO NPCs compared with WT NPCs, whereas there was no significant difference in that of other phospholipids and free fatty acids (Fig. 7E).
Treatment with LPA increased the number of bRGCs in Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids (Fig. 7F and G).

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with a homozygous PNPLA8 missense variant and prenatal-onset severe neurodegeneration, which adds to the PNPLA8-related disorder phenotype.

findings.statement: Masih et al. (2021) reported a patient with prenatal-onset severe and progressive neurodegeneration who died in infancy.
quotes: The patient had prenatal-onset severe and progressive neurodegeneration with mortality in infancy.

findings.statement: In a patient with prenatal-onset severe neurodegeneration, Masih et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous missense variant (c.1874A>G) in the patatin domain of the PNPLA8 gene.
quotes: Using whole-exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous novel missense variation c.1874A>G in the patatin domain of PNPLA8.

relevance_reason: Reports three new patients from two families with PNPLA8 variants found by exome sequencing, including a congenital-form patient and an infantile-onset phenotype. This widens the phenotypic spectrum of PNPLA8-related mitochondriopathy.

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) reported 3 patients from 2 families with PNPLA8-related mitochondriopathy. Patient 1 had the congenital form of the disease. Previously reported congenital-onset patients had congenital microcephaly, early-onset epileptic encephalopathy and early death.
quotes: Patient 1 presented with the congenital form of the disease
congenital onset displaying congenital microcephaly, early onset epileptic encephalopathy and early lethality

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) described 2 patients (Patients 2 and 3) with progressive microcephaly, seizures beginning in infancy, progressive cortical atrophy, white matter loss, bilateral basal ganglia degeneration, and cystic encephalomalacia. The authors proposed infantile onset as a new, distinct phenotype of PNPLA8-related disease.
quotes: Patients 2 and 3 showed progressive microcephaly, infantile onset seizures, progressive cortical atrophy, white matter loss, bilateral degeneration of basal ganglia, and cystic encephalomalacia
our results add the infantile onset as a new distinct phenotype of the disease

findings.statement: In Family I, Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) used exome sequencing to identify a loss-of-function variant in the PNPLA8 gene, c.1231C>T (p.Arg411Ter).
quotes: exome sequencing identified a loss of function variant (c.1231C>T, p.Arg411Ter) in Family I

findings.statement: In Family II, Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) used exome sequencing to identify a missense variant in the PNPLA8 gene, c.1559T>A (p.Val520Asp).
quotes: a missense variant (c.1559T>A, p.Val520Asp) in Family II in PNPLA8

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) suggested that age at disease onset in PNPLA8-related disorders correlates strongly with where the variant lies, not with the variant type. They described the congenital, infantile, childhood-onset and adult-onset forms as overlapping parts of a single spectrum.
quotes: suggest that the site of the variant rather than its type is strongly correlated with the disease onset
these conditions demonstrate some overlapping features representing a spectrum with clinical features always aligning with different age of onset

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) summarized earlier reports of PNPLA8 variants. These described a congenital-onset form, a childhood neurodegeneration form with progressive microcephaly, and an adult-onset form with cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy. Only 6 patients with biallelic PNPLA8 variants had been reported before.
quotes: Pathogenic variants in PNPLA8 have been described either with congenital onset displaying congenital microcephaly, early onset epileptic encephalopathy and early lethality or childhood neurodegeneration with progressive microcephaly.
a phenotype comprising adulthood onset cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy was also reported
only six patients with biallelic variants in PNPLA8 have been reported so far

relevance_reason: This is a mouse study of how PNPLA8 and PNPLA7 work in the liver. It reports Pnpla8-deficient mice but includes no human patients. It adds functional and animal-model context to the PNPLA8-related disorder.

findings.statement: Hirabayashi et al. (2023) found that PNPLA8-deficient mice reproduced most of the phenotypes of PNPLA7-deficient mice. These included growth retardation, hypoglycemia, hypolipidemia, increased energy consumption, reduced adiposity, increased FGF21, and an altered histone/DNA methylation landscape, which the authors attributed to methionine insufficiency. Unlike wildtype mice fed a methionine/choline-deficient diet, the knockout mice had decreased hepatic triglyceride. The authors suggested this was likely due to reduced lipogenesis and reduced GPC-derived glycerol flux.
quotes: accompanied by various signs of methionine insufficiency, including growth retardation, hypoglycemia, hypolipidemia, increased energy consumption, reduced adiposity, increased fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21), and an altered histone/DNA methylation landscape. Moreover, PNPLA8-deficient mice recapitulate most of these phenotypes.
both knockout strains display decreased hepatic triglyceride, likely via reductions of lipogenesis and GPC-derived glycerol flux

findings.statement: Hirabayashi et al. (2023) reported that the phospholipase/lysophospholipase pathway formed by PNPLA8 and PNPLA7 breaks down membrane phosphatidylcholine into water-soluble glycerophosphocholine (GPC) in the liver. This process makes choline stored in hepatic phosphatidylcholine available for methyl metabolism and for replenishing the methionine cycle.
quotes: the catabolism of membrane phosphatidylcholine (PC) into water-soluble glycerophosphocholine (GPC) by the phospholipase/lysophospholipase PNPLA8-PNPLA7 axis enables endogenous choline stored in hepatic PC to be utilized in methyl metabolism

relevance_reason: Reports a family with biallelic PNPLA8 loss-of-function variants and a milder adolescent-onset ataxia/neuropathy phenotype, which widens the phenotypic spectrum of PNPLA8-associated mitochondrial disease.

findings.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) described 2 adult Lithuanian siblings (a brother and a sister) whose slowly progressive ataxia began between ages 10 and 14 years. The ataxia was accompanied by progressive sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy and cognition was preserved. The brother's symptoms started at age 14 years with lower limb weakness, distal muscle atrophy, ataxia, and gait disturbance. He could not walk without assistance from age 17 years. Later he showed tetraparesis, absent lower limb reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, foot deformities, dysmetria, and distal hypoesthesia. At age 45 he had mild dysarthria and horizontal nystagmus, a normal MMSE score, and mild cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI.
quotes: Both siblings presented with adolescence-onset ataxia, progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and preserved cognition over time. The onset of symptoms was between 10 and 14 years of age.
His first symptoms occurred at the age of 14 years when he developed weakness and distal muscle atrophy of his lower limbs. These symptoms were accompanied by ataxia and gait disturbance
A neurologic examination at the age of 45 years showed mild dysarthria and horizontal nystagmus.

findings.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) reported that the sister developed walking difficulty and weakness in both lower limbs at age 14 years. When examined at age 21 she had distal limb muscle atrophy, absent lower limb reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, severe axial ataxia, and appendicular dysmetria, and she could not keep an upright posture. Her cranial nerves and cognition were normal. Nerve conduction studies showed axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and EMG showed no myopathic changes.
quotes: Sibling B developed difficulty in walking and weakness in both lower limbs at the age of 14 years.
Coordination testing revealed severe axial ataxia and appendicular dysmetria, which was more pronounced in the lower limbs.
EMG revealed sparse abnormal spontaneous activity in the distal muscles of the lower limbs without myopathic changes.

findings.statement: In 2 Lithuanian siblings with adolescent-onset ataxia and neuropathy, Burnyte et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous frameshift variants in exon 11 of PNPLA8. One was a novel deletion, c.2269del (p.Thr757GlnfsTer10), which was absent from ExAC, 1000 Genomes, and gnomAD. The other was a previously reported 2-bp deletion, c.2275_2276del (p.Leu759AlafsTer4), inherited from the mother. The father's DNA was not available, but the sequencing data showed that the 2 variants were in trans. Sanger sequencing confirmed both variants in the affected sister.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing led to the identification of the novel heterozygous deletion c.2269del (p.(Thr757Glnfs*10)) and previously reported c.2275_2276del (p.(Leu759Alafs*4)) variant in PNPLA8 (RefSeq: NM_001256007.3).
This variant is not reported in the ExAC, 1000G, or gnomAD databases. The previously described c.2275_2276del variant was maternally inherited.
results of whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing allowed us to ascertain that both changes were on different alleles (in trans)

findings.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) noted that c.2275_2276del had previously been reported, together with another truncating variant, in a patient with severe early-childhood neurodegeneration, whereas their siblings had a milder phenotype. Both truncating variants in the siblings lie in the last coding exon of PNPLA8. The authors suggested that these transcripts may escape nonsense-mediated decay and possibly retain partial enzyme activity.
quotes: Of interest, c.2275_2276del has been reported in a compound heterozygous state with other variant leading to protein truncation and resulting in severe neurodegeneration manifesting in early childhood.

Both protein-truncating variants were identified in the last coding exon of PNPLA8 gene, suggesting that such transcripts may escape nonsense-mediated decay and possibly result in preserved partial enzyme activity and less severe clinical manifestation.

relevance_reason: The paper characterizes a skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2gamma (PNPLA8) knockout mouse that recapitulates core features of the human disorder — myopathy, muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, dysmorphic mitochondria, respiratory chain deficiency and elevated lactate — and it references the human PNPLA8-null patients with mitochondrial myopathy and lactic acidosis.

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) generated a skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2gamma (PNPLA8) knockout mouse (SKMiPLA2gammaKO) by crossing mice carrying loxP sites flanking exon 5 of the iPLA2gamma gene, which encodes the enzyme active site, with transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase driven by the human alpha-actin promoter; western blot analysis of mitochondria from white adipose tissue, liver and skeletal muscle confirmed that ablation of iPLA2gamma was restricted to skeletal muscle.
quotes: To generate the skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2γ KO mouse, exon 5 (encoding the iPLA2γ active site) was flanked by loxP sites as described previously and ablated by crossing with a transgenic mouse expressing Cre-recombinase driven by the human alpha-actin promoter (The Jackson Laboratory, Cat. # 006149).

Importantly, the expression levels of the iPLA2γ isoforms in liver and white adipose tissue from the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse were unchanged in comparison to those present in WT mice (Figure 1A). In contrast, mitochondrial iPLA2γ protein expression levels in skeletal muscle tissues were nearly completely ablated in SKMiPLA2γKO mice.

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that genetic ablation of skeletal muscle iPLA2gamma in the mouse produced pronounced muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and increased blood lactate resulting from defects in mitochondrial function that impaired metabolic processing of pyruvate and caused bioenergetic inefficiency; the authors concluded that these findings established a multicomponent myopathy with pathophysiologic effects on skeletal muscle bioenergetics, mechanical function, and whole-body energy metabolism.
quotes: Genetic ablation of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ resulted in pronounced muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and increased blood lactate resulting from defects in mitochondrial function impairing metabolic processing of pyruvate and resultant bioenergetic inefficiency.

These critical roles of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ are underscored by the clear presence of a multicomponent myopathy that has pathophysiologic effects on skeletal muscle bioenergetics, mechanical function, and whole-body energy metabolism.

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found that tibialis anterior and quadriceps muscle mass was decreased by 30% in male SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice, with a greater loss of tibialis anterior mass in females; transmission electron microscopy of tibialis anterior muscle from 7-month-old knockout mice showed a prevalence of mitochondria with severe ultrastructural damage including irregular cristae and electron dense inclusions, accompanied by disruption of normal striated muscle structure.
quotes: A prominent physical difference of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse in comparison to WT controls was the decrease in the size/weight of the tibialis anterior (TA) and quadriceps (Quad) muscle groups that were decreased by 30% in male mice (Figure 1B). Examination of gender differences demonstrated a greater loss of TA mass in females in comparison to males by deletion of iPLA2γ.

TEM image analysis of the TA muscle from WT and KO mice demonstrated a prevalence of mitochondria with severe ultrastructural damage, including irregular cristae and electron dense inclusions present in the KO mouse accompanied by the disruption of normal striated muscle structure (Figures 1C and S1).

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) showed that mitochondrial DNA copy number, assessed as ND1 relative to nuclear HK2 by qPCR, was significantly decreased in SKMiPLA2gammaKO tibialis anterior muscle, and that protein levels of the mitochondrial fusion/fission proteins DRP1, OPA1 and MFN1 were dramatically diminished despite only modest decreases in their mRNA levels, whereas the ratio of recoverable mitochondrial protein to muscle mass and the mitochondrial markers VDAC, ANT and citrate synthase were unchanged.
quotes: In contrast, mtDNA copy number in SKMiPLA2γKO TA muscle was significantly decreased indicating alterations in mitochondrial content due to disrupted -mtDNA maintenance processes (Figure 1E). Furthermore, despite only modest decreases in mRNA levels of DRP1, OPA1, and MFN1 relative to WT controls, the expression levels of these proteins were dramatically diminished in SKMiPLA2γKO TA muscle, which likely contributed to the observed decrease in mtDNA copy number and the altered morphology of the mitochondria (Figures 1F and S2).

This result was supported by western blot analyses showing no significant differences in normalized expression levels of abundant mitochondrial marker proteins including VDAC, ANT, and citrate synthase (CS) from WT and iPLA2γ KO TA muscle tissue (Figure 1F).

phenotypes.text: decreased mitochondrial DNA copy number in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in muscle tissue

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that protein synthesis through the Akt/mTOR muscle growth pathway involving S6 ribosomal protein was significantly impaired in SKMiPLA2gammaKO muscle, with marked decreases in phosphorylation of these proteins despite compensatory upregulation of Akt and S6 protein mass and prominent cleavage of mTOR, while autophagic flux monitored by LC3B-I/II and p62 was unchanged; they concluded that reduced net protein synthesis in the setting of bioenergetic inefficiency likely underlay the muscle atrophy.
quotes: The results indicated that protein synthesis via the Akt/mTOR muscle growth pathway involving S6 ribosomal protein activation was significantly impaired due to dramatic decreases in phosphorylation (indicating activation) of these proteins despite compensatory upregulation of Akt and S6 protein mass (Figure 1G).

Autophagocytic flux monitored by LC3B-I/II and p62 (p62/SQSTM1) protein expression levels was not significantly changed in SKMiPLA2γKO mouse TA muscle when compared with WT controls (Figure 1G). Thus, reduction of the net rate of protein synthesis in the presence of bioenergetic inefficiency likely underlies the skeletal muscle atrophy present in the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse.

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found in grip and treadmill tests of 7- to 8-month-old mice that SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice had weaker grip force and fatigued more rapidly during treadmill exercise, irrespective of diet type or sex, and that serum lactate after treadmill exercise rose more in knockout than wild-type mice despite a shorter average exercise duration.
quotes: Both grip tests and treadmill exercise tests revealed that the iPLA2γ KO mouse had a weaker grip force and was more rapidly fatigued during treadmill exercise. These results indicate that deletion of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ resulted in compromised skeletal muscle mechanical function.
Conversely, serum lactate levels present in the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse after exercise on the treadmill increased more than WT despite a shorter average exercise duration time (Figure 2E).

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that in high-intensity treadmill exercise at 18 m/min for 4 min, 3 of 6 SKMiPLA2gammaKO female mice were completely exhausted within 1 to 2.5 min, and blood lactate accumulation markedly increased with a corresponding decline in blood glucose in the knockout compared with wild-type counterparts.
quotes: Note that 3 out of 6 KO mice were completely exhausted within 1–2.5 min and their glucose and lactate levels were measured immediately upon reaching exhaustion.

Consistent with the respiration results with isolated mitochondria, lactate accumulation in the blood of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse markedly increased with a corresponding decline in blood glucose following intense exercise in comparisons with their WT counterparts (Figures 3G and 3H).

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found that histology of tibialis anterior muscle from SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice showed internalization of nuclei and smaller myocyte diameter, with quadriceps showing irregularly sized myocytes and increased numbers of markedly smaller myofibers; myogenin expression was markedly increased while MyoD was unchanged, indicating more active regenerative myogenesis, and fast-twitch tibialis anterior muscle was further shifted toward a fast-twitch type II fiber phenotype.
quotes: TA muscle cross sections from the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse displayed internalization of nuclei and a smaller apparent myocyte diameter while those from WT had a relatively larger diameter and multiple peripheral nuclei (Figure 2H).

Although expression levels of the myogenic regulatory factor MyoD were essentially unchanged in the SKMiPLA2γKO in comparison to WT controls, markedly increased expression of Myogenin due to iPLA2γ loss of function in skeletal muscle is indicative of more active regenerative myogenesis in SKMiPLA2γKO vs. WT mice (Figure 2I).

Interestingly, fast-twitch TA muscle from the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse was further shifted toward a fast-twitch type II muscle fiber phenotype as determined by western blot analysis for fast- and slow-skeletal muscle myosin (Figure 2G).

phenotypes.text: increased number of internal/central nuclei in muscle fibers
phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) showed by ex vivo isometric force measurement of extensor digitorum longus muscle from 4 wild-type and 4 SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice that EDL muscle weight and total body weight were lower in knockouts, giving a smaller physiological cross-sectional area, but that specific tetanic peak tension after normalization to cross-sectional area did not differ between genotypes; the authors noted this limited the ability to exclude neurological or behavioral contributions to the weakness.
quotes: EDL muscle weight as well as the total body weight of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse were lower than WT controls resulting in a smaller physiological cross-sectional area (PCSA). Muscle force measurements indicated that specific tetanic peak tensions after normalization to PCSA were not different between WT and SKMiPLA2γKO mice (Figure 2F).

However, since no difference in specific force was observed, we cannot exclude the possibility of neurological and/or behavioral defects in the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse contributing to muscle weakness and atrophy.

phenotypes.text: normal specific tetanic force after normalization to cross-sectional area

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) used high-resolution respirometry of saponin-permeabilized tibialis anterior muscle and found that mitochondria from normal-chow-fed male SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice consumed 50% less oxygen than wild-type controls with glutamate/pyruvate/malate as substrate, with an even larger difference in females; protein levels of complex IV and cytochrome c were dramatically reduced, and although complex I and II protein levels were unchanged, their catalytic activities were decreased by about 50% and 25%, respectively.
quotes: Consistent with the above results, TA mitochondria isolated from SKMiPLA2γKO male mice on an NC-diet consumed 50% less oxygen than WT controls under same conditions (Figure 3A).

Interestingly, the protein expression levels of complex IV and cytochrome c in SKMiPLA2γKO skeletal muscle were dramatically reduced in comparison to WT littermates (Figure 3B). Moreover, although the expression levels of complexes I and II were not detectably altered in KO TA muscle, the individually measured activities of complexes I and II were decreased by ∼ 50% and ∼ 25%, respectively, when compared with WT controls (Figures 3C and 3D).

phenotypes.text: decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

phenotypes.text: decreased activity of mitochondrial complex II
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex II

phenotypes.text: decreased cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) protein
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex IV

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) measured mitochondrial membrane potential with a tetraphenylphosphonium electrode in mitochondria isolated from tibialis anterior muscle of 5 wild-type and 5 knockout mice and found it significantly lower in SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice with either complex I (glutamate/pyruvate/malate) or complex II (succinate) substrates, and that hydrogen peroxide production from forward and reverse electron transfer was greatly attenuated in the knockout.
quotes: The mitochondrial membrane potential in SKMiPLA2γKO mouse TA muscle with complex I or complex II substrates (i.e., glutamate/pyruvate/malate or succinate, respectively) was significantly lower than that of WT littermates (Figure 3E).

Consistent with the lower membrane potential of SKMiPLA2γKO mitochondria, hydrogen peroxide production indicative of ROS generated from forward (i.e., observed with glutamate/pyruvate/malate with rotenone) and reverse (i.e., observed with succinate) electron transfer was greatly attenuated in SKMiPLA2γKO mice in comparison with WT controls (Figure 3F).

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) used multidimensional mass spectrometry-based shotgun lipidomics and found that SKMiPLA2gammaKO tibialis anterior muscle had significantly lower levels of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin, the most abundant mature cardiolipin species in skeletal muscle, and decreased 22:6-containing cardiolipin species during normal-chow feeding; the authors suggested that loss of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin contributes to inefficient respiration by disrupting the stability and association of electron transport chain proteins.
quotes: The results indicated that SKMiPLA2γKO TA muscle possessed significantly lower levels of tetra 18:2 CL, the most abundant mature form of CL molecular species in skeletal muscle, as well as decreased 22:6-containing CL molecular species during NC feeding.

These data suggest that loss of tetra-18:2 CL contributes to inefficient respiration through disruption of the stability and/or the association of ETC proteins likely resulting from alterations in mitochondrial membrane surface charge and molecular dynamics.

phenotypes.text: abnormal cardiolipin composition of mitochondrial membrane

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found that SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice were resistant to high-fat diet-induced weight gain, gaining on average about 8 g versus about 16 g in wild-type mice after 3 months of high-fat feeding, and showed improved glucose clearance with a lower peak glucose (about 240 versus about 320 mg/dL) and decreased area under the curve during glucose challenge, without significant differences in insulin tolerance or serum insulin levels.
quotes: Specifically, the net body mass increase of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse following consumption of an HF diet was on average ∼ 8g while WT mice gained ∼ 16g after 3-month of HF feeding (Figures 5A and 5B).

In contrast, SKMiPLA2γKO mice displayed an improved response to glucose challenge resulting in a peak concentration of ∼ 240 mg glucose/dl and the decreased area under the curve during glucose challenge (Figure 5H).

Although the SKMiPLA2γKO mice exhibited a lower basal blood glucose level after HF feeding than wild-type controls, no significant differences in insulin tolerance and serum insulin levels in WT vs. KO were observed (Figures 5J and 5K).

phenotypes.text: failure to gain weight on high-fat diet

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that high-fat-fed SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice had dramatically less hepatic lipid droplet content, significantly lower hepatic triacylglycerol and diacylglycerol molecular species, no increase in liver-to-body weight ratio, diminished high-fat diet-induced fibrosis, and higher hepatic glycogen content than wild-type controls, while high-fat diet-induced increases in white adipose tissue mass were significantly more prominent in the knockout.
quotes: First, utilizing H & E staining and imaging, we found that the content of lipid droplets present in the HF-fed SKMiPLA2γKO liver was dramatically less than HF-fed WT controls (Figure 6A).
Higher amounts of glycogen were present in iPLA2γ KO liver in comparison to WT liver controls (Figure 7A).
Interestingly, HF diet-induced increases in white adipose tissue mass were significantly more prominent in SKMiPLA2γKO mice than WT controls (Figure 5D).

phenotypes.text: decreased hepatic steatosis on high-fat diet

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023) concluded that iPLA2gamma mediates skeletal muscle bioenergetic function through preservation of mitochondrial structural and functional integrity, maintenance of an appropriate membrane environment for assembly of protein complexes, and concerted signaling of skeletal muscle with the liver, and that the compromised bioenergetic and physiologic phenotype of the skeletal muscle iPLA2gamma knockout mouse was due to multifactorial mitochondrial dysfunction for which no single precipitating cause could be identified.
quotes: Collectively, the present study demonstrates that iPLA2γ mediates skeletal muscle bioenergetic function through multiple mechanisms including: 1) the preservation of mitochondrial structural and functional integrity; 2) the appropriate membrane environment (e.g., surface charge, assembly of protein complexes, mitochondrial membrane morphology for optimal mitochondria function; and 3) concerted signaling of skeletal muscle with the liver for inter-organ impedance matching to facilitate metabolic flexibility in organismal bioenergetics.

The observed mitochondrial dysfunction is multifactorial in nature and it is not possible to identify a single precipitating cause. Nevertheless, the results clearly identify that the compromised bioenergetic and physiologic phenotype of the skeletal muscle iPLA2γ KO mouse is due to mitochondrial dysfunction.

findings.statement: Moon et al. (2023), reviewing prior work motivating their study, noted that the relevance of iPLA2gamma-mediated pathologies in humans was underscored by the discovery through exome sequencing of a severely ill patient null for both iPLA2gamma alleles due to a premature stop codon in both alleles, who demonstrated marked mitochondrial morphologic alterations, muscle weakness, and lactic acidosis, and that a subsequent study reported two more unrelated patients with loss-of-function variants in PNPLA8 and similar pathologic alterations.
quotes: Furthermore, the relevance of iPLA2γ-mediated pathologies in humans was underscored by the discovery of a severely ill patient null for both iPLA2γ alleles that was identified through exome sequencing identifying a premature stop codon for iPLA2γ in both alleles. This patient demonstrated marked mitochondrial morphologic alterations, muscle weakness, and lactic acidosis.
A subsequent study reported two more unrelated patients with loss-of-function variants in PNPLA8 encoding iPLA2γ and similar pathologic alterations.

variants.as_reported: premature stop codon for iPLA2γ in both alleles

relevance_reason: Describes the metabolic and mitochondrial phenotype of iPLA2gamma (Pnpla8) knockout mice, an animal model of the gene underlying MMLA.

findings.statement: Song et al. (2010) found that iPLA2gamma-knockout mice fed a high-fat Western diet were resistant to diet-induced increases in body weight, adiposity, and blood cholesterol, glucose, and insulin, compared with wildtype mice. This occurred even though knockout and wildtype mice ate similar amounts of food and digested and absorbed dietary fat similarly. Knockout mice were also relatively resistant to diet-induced insulin resistance, glucose intolerance, and changes in fat versus carbohydrate fuel use.
quotes: We find that KO mice are resistant to WD-induced increases in body weight and adiposity and in blood levels of cholesterol, glucose, and insulin, even though WT and KO mice exhibit similar food consumption and dietary fat digestion and absorption.
KO mice are also relatively resistant to WD-induced insulin resistance, glucose intolerance, and altered patterns of fat vs. carbohydrate fuel utilization.

findings.statement: Song et al. (2010) showed that skeletal muscle from iPLA2gamma-knockout mice had impaired mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids. On a Western diet, knockout muscle and liver accumulated more long-chain acylcarnitine species than wildtype tissue. Knockout mice also excreted more long-chain acylcarnitine in urine and deposited much less triacylglycerol in the liver. The authors concluded that iPLA2gamma deficiency leads to impaired mitochondrial oxidation of fatty acids.
quotes: KO skeletal muscle exhibits impaired mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids, as reflected by accumulation of larger amounts of long-chain acylcarnitine (LCAC) species in KO muscle and liver compared with WT in response to WD feeding.
This is associated with increased urinary excretion of LCAC and much reduced deposition of triacylglycerols in liver by WD-fed KO compared with WT mice.
The iPLA(2)gamma-deficient genotype thus results in a phenotype characterized by impaired mitochondrial oxidation of fatty acids and relative resistance to the metabolic abnormalities induced by WD.
